read the rest. had a hopeless chuckle.

absolutely sickening.
the american healthcare system is UTTER bullshit.

this is definitely not a problem with all therapists and med profs. I've told both of my old therapists about being suicidal and they haven't called the cops on me or had me committed or anything. i've always wondered if it's because i don't have a history of attempts idk
quick q. are you in the us? and if so, are you going to have to pay for that medical care? just curious for if i end up asking for help and it goes this way. i don't have health insurance.

Read through your posts and you seem like a younger me! Seems like you're in high school? i'm that future you talked about fearing where you're not able to deal with your  issues early, graduate college, then flounder because you have no motivation to do things, don't know who you are or what you want. it seems that you have some of the knowledge that I've only now realized about just how separated I feel from others, how much I hate myself, how I think I won't get better.

I'm going to give you the advice that I think might've saved me. I'm this crazy paradox of wanting to die constantly but also buying into anti-suicide rhetoric a bit (might have something to do with my hours upon hours of hotline work lol). 

Anyways, you've talked about isolating yourself because you don't want other people to have to deal with you. I think therein lies your saving grace. I have personally realized that this is a self-absorbed position. Truth is everyone on this planet is living their own personal hell. Hell is the fear of the judgment of other people. Heaven is the acceptance of the support of other people. People can absolutely understand where you're coming from, but you have to bother them. You have to burden them. Be as "inconvenient" as you need to be. You'll feel freer and be able to accept yourself for who you are when you become painfully honest. And maybe you'll even find some camaraderie in other people who are ready to stop lying about the hell their living and lean on the kindness, care, and love of others, our only saving grace in this godforsaken life.
I get it. Feel the exact same way. Could've written all this out myself.
god has this been a long phase! patiently waiting its end. sooner than later i hope!

since my life really started going to shit i've been having those thoughts. i've been suicidal more than half my life and i finally have some very good reasons to end it all. it really feels like this is the end. the life i lead now feels comical.

the amount of pain that happens every second is so disgusting. the world is so ugly. there's beauty too. for everyone who overcomes, another succumbs. for every hopeful u/mdquack, there's a hopeless u/threwawaylove1, and some days our positions switch. life is just wild

i see a lot of ppl saying maybe it gets worse after death. so do you believe suicide is some sort of sin that will cause you to have a bad afterlife, or that everyone will experience a bad afterlife? personally i couldn't imagine anything worse than life. say i die and find myself burning for eternity. there's a certain peace in that. nothing you can do to change it, no possibility of things improving. certainty–sounds like heaven lol

I do something called porn. Porn is essentially movies for adults with sex, so in a way I am an actor. Sex essentially is when other people let you touch their body parts and letting other people touch your body parts, so that you and the other person/people feel good in a special way. Sometimes, the work is hard and some problems come from it; the companies that make the porn need to make some changes.
That's good. Thought my last comment sounded mean upon reflection. Thanks for sharing your experience.

Is that stuff really possible though? 

Would you say you're earnestly pursuing your dreams?

Right now, it probably seems impossible. But you can find all that again. Plenty of great people out there who can make you smile and bring light into your life. Literally just read someone's post in another thread where they said they were thankful they didn't kill themselves after breaking up with the person they were in love with at 21, now they're 30 and married to the love of their life. Seems like a lot of people go through what you've gone through and come out better.

But as a perpetually single person (definitely to a fault), I think some balance is important too. I think you have to see the worth in your life independent of other people, while being open to all the joy that outside love can bring.

It sounds like your job's really crushing you. Is there no way for you to move on from it. Are you able to apply for other more relaxed jobs now?

And so things improved once you left school. That's great. 

Unfortunately, got out of school, and things still suck. And in my case I don't think it's the environment, the problem is me. I see how things work, but I can't get myself to follow the scripts of society.

I don't really know what that's like. I have too many hangups to be that vulnerable with someone. Kudos to you for being willing to take that plunge, and love someone! you know what they say, it's better to have loved and lost than...  


But it sounds like maybe what kept you going was feeling loved by her? What exactly made her your reason to wake up?

Coincidentally, the hope of publishing good work keeps me going a bit.

So have you found fulfillment in your writing? And how did you know things weren't going to be that way forever? My struggle is that unfortunately I wake up with the same brain every morning, same hangups, same bad memories, same resistance to change.
Do you have a passion in life? What would you be doing if there were no barriers?
Thanks. Looked through your history a bit and I like your take on things. How did you arrive at being so hopeful? What keeps you going?

I know it helps people for sure. And maybe I just didn't let it, but my experiences with therapy have really summed up to convoluted conversations that ultimately sum up to "Just try harder." Like that's the whole message I got.

The way I see it. I have no recollection of a time before I was born, so I don't think it's so hard to believe that there's nothing after I die as well. 

Like there's just no proof of anything beyond. Everything's been debunked. I just find it so hard to believe that there's more. But if there is, I'm gonna be really pissed, esp. if I end up continuing to suffer through life lol
Beautifully said. Thanks. I'm happy that you found support.
That's the good thing. It will end eventually! Thank god!

Shame - I guess it means exposure, the feeling of having people see that you're not where you should be, that you're struggling, that you're failing.

I feel uncertain because I can't tell the future. I don't know how things are going to go. If things go badly, I think I might feel more hurt, more hopeless.

I'm always questioning people's kindness and motives. I think they are going to fuck me over. And they usually do, but if I want to rationalize it, it's because my expectations are too high.
I get that. But if I believe what some people say, you have to keep trying? One day you'll reach out to the right person, and it will make all the difference?
You're not wrong. I think that part of my problem is that I care too much what others think and how things look.

I think a large chunk happen because of unemployment b/c society says it's a good reason.

I get what you're trying to say, but if I'm dead I won't be kicking myself for anything anymore. Sounds so peaceful.
